title: Judging the Justification: Decision Certificate Supervision for Generative Reward Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.27528v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Generative reward models (GenRMs) generate natural language rationales to justify preference judgments, yet a correct verdict does not guarantee a sound justification. Existing approaches often rely on reference explanations to supervise rationales, but obtaining such references can be costly and does not necessarily establish whether generated rationales support the resulting verdict. To address these limitations, we propose DeCert, a framework that evaluates the validity and verdict consistency of generated rationales without requiring reference explanations. Crucially, DeCert translates these assessments into preference supervision that accounts for both verdict correctness and justification quality. In particular, when multiple sampled judgments share the same correct verdict, differences in certificate quality enable DeCert to construct rationale preference pairs that distinguish stronger from weaker justifications. translated_title: 评判理由的正当性：面向生成式奖励模型的决策证书监督
translated_abstract: 生成式奖励模型通过生成自然语言理由来论证其偏好判断，然而正确的结论并不保证理由本身是可靠的。现有方法通常依赖参考解释来监督理由的生成，但获取这类参考代价高昂，且未必能确定生成的理由是否真正支持最终的结论。为解决这些局限，我们提出了DeCert，一个无需参考解释即可评估生成理由的有效性及其与结论一致性的框架。关键在于，DeCert将这些评估转化为同时考虑结论正确性与理由质量的偏好监督信号。特别地，当多个采样判断具有相同的正确结论时，证书质量的差异使DeCert能够构建理由偏好对，从而区分更强与更弱的理由论证。大量实验证明了……
tldr: 提出DeCert框架，无需参考解释即可评估生成式奖励模型所生成理由的有效性与结论一致性，并将其转化为兼顾结论正确性和理由质量的偏好监督信号，以区分强弱的理由论证。
en_tdlr: DeCert is a framework that supervises generative reward models by evaluating the validity and verdict consistency of generated rationales without reference explanations, converting these assessments into preference supervision that distinguishes stronger from weaker justifications.
